html:
The Nauo, also spelt Nawu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southwest of Eyre Peninsula in South Australia.

Their neighbours were the Barngarla to the east and the Wirangu up the west coast. Port Lincoln was founded on the peninsula in 1839, and sheep runs and violence on the frontier followed in the 1840s. Many survivors were drawn to the Poonindie mission near Port Lincoln, opened in 1850.

The Nauo language was no longer spoken by the twentieth century, but descendants are now working to revive it.
sum: The Nauo, also spelt Nawu, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the southwest of Eyre Peninsula in South Australia.
